subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Elevator: Otis's Safety Brake
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Elevator: Otis's Safety Brake.

hook.text: Elevators existed before Otis. People were just too scared to ride them.

buildup.text: If the rope broke, the platform fell. No safety net, no survival.

discovery.text: Otis added spring-loaded clamps that grabbed guide rails if the rope snapped.

twist.text: He proved it at a fair by cutting the rope himself — the crowd gasped, then cheered.

climax.text: Safe elevators made skyscrapers possible. Cities grew up, not just out.

punchline.text: One safety brake reshaped every city skyline on Earth.

quiz.question: How did Otis's invention change cities?
options: It made building construction faster and cheaper
Safe elevators made tall buildings practical, enabling skyscrapers
It replaced stairs entirely in all buildings
